title: Evidence for Chapter 31: Soviet industrialization, the famine of 1930-1934 and the socialist calculation debate, 1917-1945

(1936); the Soviet Union Information Bureau (1929); Mises (1920, in Hayek ed. 1935); Lange (1938); Hayek (1945); Markevich, Naumenko and Qian (NBER WP 29089); Rudnytskyi et al. notes: Every quotation is checked word for word against the cached source text by data/fetch/verify_web_quotes.py, and every value is read from its quotation by checks/check_ch31.py; rows with an empty quotation are values or words read on a page image (sources gosplan1933img, sc1936, mnq2021img, harrison1993), named as such in their notes, which give a transcription between « and »; the whole panel II of the image table of Markevich, Naumenko and Qian is the table snapshot soviet_grain. The OCR texts keep their misreadings as printed and the notes name them: 'incr@ised', 'thé', '34.3.' (gosplan1933), '11,6' with a decimal comma and 'Livericut' (gosplan1929), 'Sozialzvissenschaften' (mises1935), 'hoo\' and 'Nos. i and 2' (lange1938); the transcription of Table A.2 keeps the table's own 'Davis'. Indirect testimony: Conquest (1986), Davies and Wheatcroft (2009), Kondrashin (2008), Polyakov and Zhiromskaya (2000), Meslé et al. (2013) and Viola (1996) through Markevich, Naumenko and Qian; Stalin's letter to Kaganovich of 11 August 1932 through the same; Stalin's telegram of 22 January 1933, Kondrashin's estimate for the Volga and the Politburo's decision of 6 December 1928 through Werth (2016); The New York Times and The Daily Telegraph of November 1932 through Stalin's report of 7 January 1933 (rows st_gamble, st_telegraph, st_nyt: the English of the report's translators, not the newspapers' own wording); Preobrazhensky and Holland Hunter through Harrison (1980); Allen (2003), Bergson, Chapman and Wheatcroft through Davies (2004) and Markevich and Harrison (2011); Khanin (1987, 1991), Moorsteen and Powell (1966), Nutter (1962) and Bergson (1961) through Harrison (1993); Rostowski and Shapiro (1991) through Harrison and Markevich (2018); Gisser and Jonas (1974) through Harrison (1980); Bergson (1964) through Gregory and Harrison (2005); Trotsky and Lange through Hayek (1945). Witnesses that disagree: the New Economic Policy announced in March 1921 (Harrison 2017; Markevich and Harrison 2011; Harrison and Markevich 2018) or 'April, 1921' (Soviet Union Information Bureau 1929); stabilization 'only in 1923' (Harrison 2017) or with the currency reform of March 1924 (the Bureau); the 'Ural-Siberian method' of January 1928 (Werth) or after the 1928 harvest (Davies); heavy industry 108 per cent of the plan (Stalin) or 103.4 per cent for group A and 109.6 per cent for the Commissariat of Heavy Industry (Gosplan 1933); oil and gas in 1932 22.2 million tons (Gosplan's text) or 22.29 (its table); the plan's variants 'basic' and 'maximum' (the English edition of 1929) or 'optimal' (Markevich and Harrison); the death toll of the famine (see the chapter's note on sources). Not obtained: Allen (2003) itself (Princeton UP answered 403), Davies and Wheatcroft (2004, 2009), Conquest (1986), Khanin's own articles, Moorsteen and Powell (1966), the Russian originals of the plan documents (Russian statistical sites unreachable), the Mises Institute's edition of Mises (1920) (403).
